description: Combined PRD evidence from two isolated Codex/Ralph stream worktrees. Verification and PR gate run on this integration branch.

userStories.title: MCP Resource Subscription Handshake
userStories.story: As an MCP client, I want Weave to advertise and handle resource subscription requests for known ontology, ObjectType, and temporary ObjectSet resources so agents can prepare for schema-change notifications without treating subscribe as unsupported.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an MCP client initializes, when it reads capabilities.resources, then subscribe is true while listChanged remains false.
Given a valid resource URI, when the client calls resources/subscribe, then the server returns an empty success result and remembers the subscription idempotently.
Given a subscribed URI, when the client calls resources/unsubscribe, then the server returns an empty success result and removes the subscription idempotently.
Given a malformed URI or unknown resource URI, when the client calls resources/subscribe, then the server returns a JSON-RPC error instead of silently succeeding.
Given the public MCP docs and CI status checks, then they describe resources/subscribe and resources/unsubscribe without stale subscribe=false claims.
dependencies: pkg/mcp resources/read URI validation and fake test repository
docs/mcp.md and scripts/ci/ci_workflow_bdd_test.go MCP status assertions

userStories.title: MCP Resource List Cursor Safety
userStories.story: As an MCP client connected to a large Weave tenant, I want resources/list to honor a cursor and deterministic page boundary so resource discovery does not require loading every ontology and ObjectType in one unbounded response.
acceptanceCriteria: Given a small page size in test wiring, when resources/list is called, then it returns a stable URI-sorted page and nextCursor.
Given a nextCursor from the first page, when resources/list is called again, then it returns the remaining resources without duplicates.
Given a malformed cursor, when resources/list is called, then it returns CodeInvalidParams.
Given no cursor or page size, existing clients still receive the full catalogue by default.
dependencies: P2A-001 subscription methods must not change resource URI ordering.

userStories.title: MCP HTTP Bridge Timeout Reliability
userStories.story: As a local MCP client using cmd/weave-mcp as a stdio bridge, I want upstream HTTP stalls to become bounded JSON-RPC errors so the client does not hang indefinitely when the Weave server is slow or unreachable.
acceptanceCriteria: Given WEAVE_MCP_URL points at a stalled endpoint, when cmd/weave-mcp forwards a request, then the bridge returns a JSON-RPC server error within the configured timeout.
Given WEAVE_MCP_HTTP_TIMEOUT is set to a valid duration, then the bridge uses that timeout.
Given WEAVE_MCP_HTTP_TIMEOUT is invalid, then startup fails clearly instead of silently using an unintended timeout.
Given existing auth env vars, then Authorization and X-Weave-API-Key forwarding keep their current precedence.

userStories.title: Localize Dashboard Ontology Card Object-Type Counts
userStories.asA: Weave operator using the browser dashboard
userStories.iWant: ontology cards to display object-type counts with the same pluralization and locale behavior as the rest of the dashboard
userStories.soThat: the landing page remains trustworthy in English and zh-CN when counts are singular, plural, or localized
acceptanceCriteria: Given an ontology card has one object type, When the dashboard renders in English, Then the chip says '1 object type' rather than '1 types'.
Given an ontology card has multiple object types, When the dashboard renders in English, Then the chip says '<count> object types'.
Given the active locale is zh-CN, When an ontology card renders, Then the chip uses dashboard.objectTypeCount translations instead of hardcoded English text.

userStories.title: Polish Schema Graph Count Copy
userStories.asA: ontology administrator reviewing the schema graph
userStories.iWant: type/link summaries to use correct singular/plural copy
userStories.soThat: the graph summary does not show awkward states like '1 types'
acceptanceCriteria: Given the schema graph has one object type and zero links, When the admin page renders, Then the summary uses singular '1 type' and plural-safe '0 links'.
Given the schema graph has multiple object types and one link, When the admin page renders, Then the summary uses '<n> types · 1 link'.
